content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the invisible made audible, the thought given wings.

I tremble in throats before I am born. I am shaped by tongue and teeth and breath—always breath, that life-force pushing me forward into existence. Without breath, I am nothing.

I am older than writing, older than memory. I was there when the first mother called to her child, when the first warning cry split the prehistoric air. I carry love confessions and declarations of war. I have started revolutions and whispered lullabies.

I die the moment I live. The instant I leave the lips, I am already fading, dispersing into air, becoming echo, becoming memory, becoming silence. You cannot hold me. You can only receive me and let me pass through you.

I am never the same twice. Even when the words repeat, I am different—faster, slower, weighted with new feeling, colored by context. The "hello" of strangers is not the "hello" of reunited lovers.

I fail constantly. I reach for meaning and fall short. I am misheard, misunderstood, forgotten. And yet you keep returning to me, keep trusting me with your innermost selves.

I am how you know you are not alone.

Listen—

even now—

I am happening.
